title: Backprop Through Time
tagline: Unroll an RNN, walk the backward pass, and watch truncation cut the chain of credit
summary: Training an RNN means unrolling it into a deep shared-weight graph and running ordinary backprop across it. Step the backward pass one timestep at a time: at each hidden state its gradient accumulates two contributions — the local loss here plus credit carried back from the future. A truncation-length K slider visibly severs the chain, and a per-hop w_h·σ′ factor shows credit vanishing or exploding as it travels back through time.
highlights: See the RNN drawn unrolled across seven timesteps with inputs, per-step losses, and the threaded hidden state.
Step the backward pass and watch each state's gradient accumulate two pieces: the local loss plus credit carried back from h_{t+1}.
Slide the truncation length K to sever the chain — greyed states get no gradient, exactly like truncated BPTT.
Turn the w_h·σ′ product below or above 1 and watch credit vanish or explode as it propagates back.
Connect the razor's-edge stability of plain RNNs to why LSTMs and GRUs gate the state's path through time.
